```markdown
# User Data Export — Implementation Tasks

Target: ship next week.

## Assumptions (from plan gaps — adjust if the meeting decided otherwise)
- Format: JSON (assumed: easiest to produce and consume; one file per export).
- "All of a user's data": every table/store keyed to the user ID (assumed).
- Delivery: async job + download link (assumed). This keeps the endpoint fast regardless of data size.
- Who can export: the authenticated user, for their own data only (assumed).

## 1. Data inventory (Day 1)
- [ ] 1.1 List every table, collection, and blob store that holds user-linked data
- [ ] 1.2 Note the join key for each source (user_id, email, etc.)
- [ ] 1.3 Flag fields to exclude: password hashes, internal security/fraud flags, other users' PII
- [ ] 1.4 Get a quick sign-off on the inventory list from the PM/data owner

## 2. API endpoints (Days 1–2)
- [ ] 2.1 `POST /api/v1/users/me/export` creates an export job and returns `202` with a job ID
- [ ] 2.2 `GET /api/v1/users/me/export/{jobId}` returns status (`pending | running | complete | failed`) and a download URL when complete
- [ ] 2.3 Require authentication and scope to the caller's own user ID (no user ID in the path)
- [ ] 2.4 Return `404` (not `403`) for job IDs the caller doesn't own
- [ ] 2.5 Rate limit: one active export per user and N per day

## 3. Export job (Days 2–3)
- [ ] 3.1 Background worker that runs one collector per data source from 1.1
- [ ] 3.2 Stream and paginate reads so large accounts don't load into memory
- [ ] 3.3 Serialize to JSON with a top-level manifest (`exported_at`, `user_id`, `schema_version`, `sections`)
- [ ] 3.4 Include referenced files/attachments as a zip, or as links, if any exist
- [ ] 3.5 Set a job timeout and retries; mark the job `failed` with an error code

## 4. Storage and delivery (Day 3)
- [ ] 4.1 Write output to private object storage, encrypted at rest
- [ ] 4.2 Serve downloads via short-lived signed URLs (e.g. 15 min)
- [ ] 4.3 Auto-delete export files after a retention window (e.g. 7 days)
- [ ] 4.4 Optional: notify the user by email or in-app when the export is ready

## 5. Security and audit (Day 4)
- [ ] 5.1 Audit-log each export request and each download (user, time, IP)
- [ ] 5.2 Optional: require recent re-authentication before an export can start
- [ ] 5.3 Test that user A cannot access user B's job or file

## 6. Performance (Day 4)
- [ ] 6.1 Benchmark against the largest real-world account size (seed data)
- [ ] 6.2 Confirm the request endpoints respond in < 200 ms (all work is async)
- [ ] 6.3 Add indexes on user_id for any slow collector queries

## 7. Testing (Days 4–5)
- [ ] 7.1 Unit tests for each collector and the serializer
- [ ] 7.2 Integration test for the full flow: request → job → download → file contents
- [ ] 7.3 Edge cases: empty account, very large account, deleted/partial records, concurrent requests
- [ ] 7.4 Verify excluded fields (1.3) never appear in the output

## 8. Release (Day 5)
- [ ] 8.1 Put the feature behind a flag; enable it internally first
- [ ] 8.2 Add metrics: job duration, failure rate, file size
- [ ] 8.3 Add alerts on job failure rate
- [ ] 8.4 Write a short API doc and support/FAQ note
- [ ] 8.5 Ramp the flag up to 100%
```

The section 1 inventory is the riskiest part of this timeline. If it turns up more sources than expected, cut 4.4 and 5.2 first.
